newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia to vote on constitutional change.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia to vote on constitutional change.

text.p: The Slovenian parliament is set to vote on Monday on amending its constitution in line with European Union demands in order to qualify for inclusion in the first round of the EU expansion.
Parliament must change the constitution to enable foreigners to own land as a precondition for ratification of the association agreement with the EU, signed in June last year.
"I expect that today we will successfully end this important and hard political step and thus open ourselves to a place in the European Union," Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek told parliament.
Last week European Commission officials said Slovenia could start negotiations on full EU membership early next year, providing it immediately ratified the EU association accord.

Analysts said the vote was likely to be passed by the necessary two-third majority since parliamentary parties had recently agreed to change the constitution by July 15 and ratify the association accord soon afterwards.
Slovenia introduced the current constitution in June 1991 after declaring independence from former Yugoslavia.
